findings.description: The test `denies the tools that open a screen pup cannot answer` also asserts the rewritten session-protocol line in `contextMarkdown`. That is a second behaviour under a name that covers only the deny rule. `docs/conventions/testing.md` line 88 says "One logical assertion focus per test. A test verifies a single behaviour". Its next line says to name the test after the behaviour. Moving the protocol-line `expect` into its own `it` would fix both.

The new comment over the `compileProfile` test repeats the decision and the JSDoc, and adds no WHY. Both the `UNANSWERABLE_TOOLS` JSDoc and decision 74 already say this. Reduce it to `// Decision 74.` or delete it.

The `UNANSWERABLE_TOOLS` JSDoc retells the mechanism already in decision 74: no input box, steer refused, watchdog never resumes. Two facts are not in the name and are worth keeping: a deny rule removes the tool from the toolset, and the conductor gets the same list. Trim it to those two facts plus the pointer.

Decision 74 is long for a one-rule change. The sentence "A turn that ends goes through the Stop hook and reads as a turn pup and the operator can see" adds little, and the verification paragraph could be shorter. Keep the `claude -p` aside and the closing "Re-run the two-pane check", which carry a real WHY and a maintenance instruction.

It describes `.claude/settings.json` as "(hooks)", but the compiled file now also carries `permissions.deny`. Decision 74 covers it and wins over 00–08, so this is only a stale parenthetical for the pending decisions-to-docs merge-back.

process_issues.description: review-maintainability was not spawned: the code change is a 13-line constant plus two settings keys and adds no structural logic. Correctness, security, conventions, docs and context covered the diff.
